chosen.premise: Jolteon’s lungs contain an electricity-making organ, so its breath crackles when it exhales.
chosen.hook: Jolteon’s lungs don’t just move air—they make electricity.
chosen.visualIdea: A cutaway of Jolteon’s lungs reveals a glowing organ, followed by crackling breath.
chosen.note: The lung-based electricity organ and crackling exhalation are highly distinctive, concrete, and directly stated in multiple Pokédex entries. The internal cutaway is an effective visual hook.

candidates.premise: Jolteon’s lungs contain an electricity-making organ, so its breath crackles when it exhales.
candidates.hook: Jolteon’s lungs don’t just move air—they make electricity.
candidates.visualIdea: A cutaway of Jolteon’s lungs reveals a glowing organ, followed by crackling breath.
candidates.note: The lung-based electricity organ and crackling exhalation are highly distinctive, concrete, and directly stated in multiple Pokédex entries. The internal cutaway is an effective visual hook.

candidates.premise: When agitated, Jolteon straightens its charged fur and fires the bristles like a missile barrage.
candidates.hook: Jolteon doesn’t just shock enemies—it shoots its fur at them.
candidates.visualIdea: Jolteon’s soft silhouette transforms into needle-like fur, then launches bristles in volleys.
candidates.note: A genuinely unexpected combat mechanic: Jolteon can straighten and fire its electrically charged bristles. The transformation and barrage are easy to depict.

candidates.premise: Jolteon turns every mood change—sadness or anger—into stored electrical power.
candidates.hook: For Jolteon, getting upset is literally a power-up.
candidates.visualIdea: Jolteon’s mood flips from happy to angry as an electricity meter charges higher.
candidates.note: The mood-to-electricity mechanic is unusually specific to Jolteon and directly supported, though the emotional meter is an interpretation rather than a literal visual shown in the games.

candidates.premise: Jolteon’s cells make only weak electricity, but static in its fur amplifies it into thunderbolts.
candidates.hook: Jolteon starts with weak power and turns it into thunderbolts.
candidates.visualIdea: Small sparks from Jolteon’s cells flow into its fur, swell, and become a massive thunderbolt.
candidates.note: The weak-electricity-to-thunderbolt escalation is well supported and visual, but it overlaps with a familiar electric-Pokémon power-up idea and is less uniquely Jolteon than its breath or fur weapons.

candidates.premise: Jolteon combines atmospheric negative ions with needle-like fur to control 10,000-volt attacks.
candidates.hook: Jolteon’s fur is part lightning rod, part weapon.
candidates.visualIdea: Negative ions gather around Jolteon while its fur rises into charged needles beneath a 10,000-volt label.
candidates.note: The 10,000-volt figure and needle-like fur are supported, but “part lightning rod” is figurative and the angle combines several facts without one especially sharp contradiction or mechanic.

candidates.premise: Eevee becomes Jolteon specifically through a Thunder Stone, choosing electricity over water, fire, or friendship.
candidates.hook: One stone decides whether Eevee becomes Jolteon instead of another evolution.
candidates.visualIdea: Eevee stands before Water, Thunder, and Fire Stones while branching paths show different evolution requirements.
candidates.note: The branching evolution visual is clear and factually supported, but Thunder Stone evolution is familiar and the “choosing” language anthropomorphizes a game mechanic.

rounds.request: N/A—electric-breath is strong enough; stronger alternatives would need an equally Jolteon-specific internal mechanic, a surprising concrete rule, and direct Pokédex support.
